name: OpenAI Agents SDK for TypeScript
tagline: A TypeScript SDK for agent workflows, tools, handoffs, tracing, and realtime applications.
hook: Requires every rendered TypeScript example to come from a compilable source file, so documentation snippets share the package’s verification workflow.
summary: The JavaScript Agents SDK guide covers conditional skills, documentation risk, supported contracts, and architecture references. Reviews must prove behavior where it is owned without expanding a change to unsupported cases.

techniques.title: Compile the examples that readers see
techniques.body: Rendered TypeScript and TSX snippets must live under examples/docs and be imported into MDX as raw source. The required build-check ties the displayed example to a maintained, compilable file.
techniques.quote: Do not add ad hoc TypeScript or TSX fenced blocks directly to MDX.

techniques.title: Classify documentation checks by the complete diff
techniques.body: Editorial, Content, and Structural tiers distinguish wording changes from changed claims, snippet wiring, navigation, and generators. The highest applicable tier determines focused checks across all task-owned files.
techniques.quote: Classify the complete task-owned diff, including committed, staged, unstaged, and task-owned untracked files, by the highest applicable documentation risk tier.

techniques.title: Look for stale ownership at asynchronous boundaries
techniques.body: The review rules call out awaits, callbacks, retries, reconnects, cleanup, and rollback as places where older work can corrupt surviving work. A finding must identify the concrete interleaving and missing invariant where the mutation occurs.
techniques.quote: When changed code mutates shared state across an `await`, callback, retry, reconnect, cancellation, cleanup, or rollback boundary, check whether stale or failing work can overwrite, revert, or dispose state owned by surviving work.

techniques.title: Keep persisted data from granting runtime authority
techniques.body: Serialized state, manifests, and provider data are not automatically trusted to control host-owned security, identity, or cleanup decisions. The guide requires a supported trust boundary before allowing those values to influence side effects.
techniques.quote: Preserve trusted current configuration and validate untrusted state before it can affect side effects, replay, or resource ownership.

techniques.title: Make a runtime finding prove a supported consequence
techniques.body: Review comments must connect changed code to incorrect behavior on a supported path. A constructible typed value, alternate semantic preference, or imagined symmetry does not establish a defect on its own.
techniques.quote: Report a runtime defect only when the changed code causes a concrete incorrect behavior on a supported path.

techniques.title: Reuse scripted doubles except at their fidelity limit
techniques.body: The testing section names common doubles for models, realtime transports, and sandbox sessions. Specialized replacements need a documented boundary such as wire conversion, controlled concurrency, or exact abort delivery that the shared utilities cannot represent.
techniques.quote: For provider-neutral agent workflow tests, prefer `ScriptedModel` over a new mock or fake `Model`.

steal: Render documentation examples from compilable source files.
Choose documentation checks using the highest risk in the whole diff.
Review asynchronous mutations for stale ownership.
Distinguish persisted values from trusted runtime authority.
Require supported, observable consequences in review findings.
Document why a specialized test double needs more fidelity.
